short_answer: The Prez is a real, active product on WagerTalk, a Las Vegas pick marketplace with written terms and a mailing address. His profile posts picks every day, prices every package, and shows a table of his last 20 graded plays. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money over time is a separate question, and nothing we could open answers it. The sales copy leads with runs such as "37-23 and 53-32" and "8-1 to star the year" in college basketball, each starting on a date the seller chose. The Last 20 table on the same profile showed 9 wins and 11 losses on 16 Nov 2026.

WagerTalk itself describes The Prez as one of its co-founders, so the marketplace that grades and promotes his record is not a neutral party. We found almost no independent buyer posts about him. Treat the numbers as marketing until you have tracked his picks yourself.

guarantee: WagerTalk sells most daily cards in two versions: a plain price and a higher "Guaranteed" price ($29.00 versus $44.00 for the Monday card we saw). The site says the guarantee "backs your purchase with 100% in credits." If the daily package does not show an overall profit, the paid value is credited to your WagerTalk account for a future purchase. It is not cash back.

The WagerTalk terms say the company's entire liability is "a refund of the price paid or replacement of our products, at our option." We saw no guarantee attached to the multi day or season passes. Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves, which are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: The bio is not consistent. The profile says he has been beating books "for the better part of two decades," while the same bio on the WagerTalk experts page says "the better part of a decade." Both versions call him an "NFL Expert" and mention "National League Football profits." We could not open who2beton.com, the site the bio says he founded.

No real name appears on the profile. A WagerTalk bio for another handicapper calls The Prez "one of our co-founders at Wagertalk," and a 2018 WagerTalk press release names Lawrence Prezman as a co-founder.

Every streak starts where the seller chose to start it, and "units" depend on how big each bet is rated. The Last 20 table on the same profile, also graded by WagerTalk, showed 9 wins and 11 losses for the plays released 10 Nov to 15 Nov 2026.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick by The Prez kept by a third party, no contest results, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: a Last 20 table, a Hot Streaks box and a Who's Hot leaderboard for the last 3, 7 and 30 days. On 16 Nov 2026 the leaderboard put him first in one sport for the last 30 days at 8-1, and the Last 20 table showed 9 wins and 11 losses across NFL, college football, college basketball, NBA and NHL plays. All of these are graded by WagerTalk, the company that sells the picks and that its own copy says he helped found.

He also posts free picks with written analysis on the profile, and the WagerTalk social account announces them several times a week. Free picks are a fair way to judge his reasoning, but a handful of them is not a record.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no pick history from The Prez is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how The Prez performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his WagerTalk pages run from 62% to 89% winners. On the Watchdog board on 16 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence about The Prez is close to nonexistent. Most public posts that mention him are WagerTalk's own free pick announcements. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found one independent post that speaks to The Prez himself: a 2026 post on X from someone who said they had known him since his Who2BetOn days and had invested in that venture, made no money, but found him honest. Everything else is about WagerTalk as a whole. A 2024 Reddit post, a 2026 TheRX post and several CapperTek reviews from buyers of other WagerTalk handicappers describe losing after purchase, and TheRX forum bars all WagerTalk cappers from its free service play threads. None of those posts names The Prez, so they say nothing about his picks in particular. We found no positive buyer report about his paid packages either.

A user on X wrote that they had known The Prez since he ran Who2BetOn before WagerTalk, that they invested in it and did not make any money, but that he was honest. No details or figures were given, and we could not verify the account.

On Reddit, a buyer posted a warning about WagerTalk in general, saying they had tried several different handicappers there, contacted support, and found all of them poor. The post does not name The Prez and gives no results.
CapperTek lists more than a dozen reviews of WagerTalk.com. The ones we read describe advertised records that did not hold up after purchase. None of the visible reviews mentions The Prez.

TheRX daily service play threads tell members not to post picks from a list of services, and the list starts with "All Wagertalk Cappers." The thread gives no reason, and it is a forum rule, not a judgment on any one handicapper.
Searches of the Reddit archive, TheRX and the web found no thread reviewing The Prez by name, and no buyer posting a long record of his paid picks. The site who2beton.com did not load for us.

conflicts: WagerTalk grades The Prez's picks, ranks him on its own leaderboards and sells his packages. A WagerTalk bio for another handicapper calls him one of the company's co-founders. The records on his profile therefore come from the seller's side of the deal.

The free picks he posts double as advertising for paid packages, and the WagerTalk site also runs sportsbook promo code pages. That proves nothing about his picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.
strengths: Sold through a company with a Las Vegas mailing address and written terms.
Every package has a published price, and daily cards come with an optional credit guarantee.
He posts free picks with full written reasoning, and the profile shows a Last 20 table that includes losses.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a streak, a short window or a total chosen by the seller.
WagerTalk describes him as one of its co-founders, so the grading and the rankings are not independent.
The guarantee pays in site credit, only on daily packages, never in cash.
The bio says two decades on one page and one decade on another, and the profile gives no real name.
We found almost no independent buyer reports, positive or negative, about his paid picks.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, active WagerTalk handicapper with published prices, daily picks and a company address behind the sales. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only records on show are graded by WagerTalk itself, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does The Prez cost?

On 16 Nov 2026 a two pick daily card cost $29.00, or $44.00 with the credit guarantee. Passes ran $39.00 for a day, $99.00 for a week, $299.00 for 30 days and $1,999.00 for a year, with a one payment year promotion at $1188.00.
Does The Prez have a verified record?

No. His profile shows streaks such as 37-23 and 53-32, leaderboard ranks and a Last 20 table that stood at 9 wins and 11 losses on 16 Nov 2026, all graded by WagerTalk. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

For the money you get every play he releases in the period you buy, with written analysis, and on guaranteed daily cards a credit if the day loses. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
